coverage_note: PARTIAL COVERAGE PASS. The full runbook (Free ~680 lines / Pro ~348 lines, 200+ discrete contract rows across A-F + S1-S26) exceeds what one session can walk exhaustively with full rigor. This run prioritized: pre-flight DB/schema/cap checks (A), the explicitly flagged 'areas changed today' (credits, reviews, member blocking, admin notices, listing types, sitemap toggle, onboarding), a handful of high-signal C/S rows, and debug.log diffing. Rows not executed are recorded as skipped, not assumed passing. See manual_required[] for the largest gaps (B upgrade path, F cross-browser, most of E/S, most D regression rows).

failures.triage_note: HIGH severity, high confidence. Reproduced live on subscriber3 (user_id 5, 32 rows in wp_listora_favorites). Root cause confirmed via DB schema: wp_listora_favorites has composite PK (user_id, listing_id) + created_at + collection -- NO id column. blocks/user-dashboard/render.php:325 runs 'SELECT listing_id FROM {prefix}favorites WHERE user_id = %d ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT %d OFFSET %d' -- the id DESC clause references a column that does not exist. WordPress logs a raw DB error and the query returns nothing, so the Favorites tab body always renders the empty state even though the tab badge (driven by a separate COUNT(*) query) correctly shows 32. Contradictory UI results: 'No saved listings' empty-state copy renders simultaneously with 'Page 1 of 2' pagination controls for a list with zero visible rows. Likely introduced in the 1.5.0 LST-F-06 dashboard-tab-pagination wave (favorites pagination copy-pasted the id DESC tiebreak pattern from reviews/claims queries, which do have an id column). Same bug class as the historical D.dashboard-stats-transient-bust (stat tile disagrees with the list underneath).
failures.expected: Favorites tab lists the member's saved listings (32 cards, paginated), matching the '32' badge count on the Favorites nav tab.
failures.actual: Favorites tab renders the empty state ('No saved listings — Save listings you like by clicking the heart icon. Browse the directory') alongside 'Page 1 of 2' pagination, while the nav tab badge correctly reads 'Favorites 32'. debug.log records: "WordPress database error Unknown column 'id' in 'order clause' for query SELECT listing_id FROM wp_listora_favorites WHERE user_id = 7 ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 0" (also reproduced for user_id 1 and 5).

failures.triage_note: MEDIUM severity. Reproduced on the dashboard Profile tab after unblocking the only blocked member. Section 'Blocked Members' renders its heading + description + an EMPTY <ul class="listora-dashboard__blocked-list"> with no fallback copy -- verified this is server-rendered (persists across a fresh page load, not just a stale client-side re-render after the AJAX unblock). Violates the plugin's own empty-state convention (used everywhere else -- directory grid, favorites, claims all render a canonical empty-state card/message).
failures.expected: With zero blocked members, the section shows an empty-state message (e.g. 'You haven't blocked anyone.') consistent with the plugin's other empty states.
failures.actual:
...
    -- blank list, no message, reads as broken/unfinished rather than genuinely empty.

failures.triage_note: LOW-MEDIUM severity, UX consistency finding, not a hard contract violation (no native window.confirm/alert/prompt fired, so the cross-cutting 'no native dialogs' check is technically satisfied). Clicking 'Block <name>' on a review card fires POST /listora/v1/me/blocks immediately (verified 201 Created in Network tab) with zero confirmation step and the review vanishes from the list instantly with no toast/success message and no visible Undo. Every other consequential action in this codebase (Deactivate Listing, per CLAUDE.md 2026-04-30 change f69f47f) routes through window.listoraConfirm() before executing. Blocking a member is comparably consequential (hides their content bidirectionally per the plugin's own copy: 'Blocking works in both directions') and arguably deserves the same confirm-then-act pattern for consistency, plus some inline feedback so the member knows the action succeeded.
failures.expected: Clicking Block prompts a listoraConfirm() modal ('Block <name>? You will no longer see their reviews...') before the REST call fires, and/or shows a success toast with an Undo action afterward.
failures.actual: Block executes immediately on click with no confirmation and no post-action feedback; the review row simply disappears.
